title: Hosted API: implement failure grace-window + customer fast-path to contain retry storms during escalations
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers escalated after observing cascading 5xx/timeouts during transient upstream slowdowns. Symptoms included synchronized client retries, spike in outgoing RPC latency, and frontdoor connection pileup. This ticket implements a short 'grace-window' circuit policy and a per-tenant fast-path guard to reduce retry amplification and preserve capacity for prioritized customer bridges during live escalations.

Context & impact: Over the last month several incident postmortems pointed to short-lived backend slowdowns that generated a wave of client retries. Our existing circuit-breakers tripped too quickly for some flows or too late for others; once tripped, fallbacks triggered heavy routing changes that increased tail latency and produced customer-visible 502/504 errors. Customers in P1 escalations need a temporary 'fast-path' that reduces their effective admission checks and prevents them from being swept up in tenant-wide backoffs while we remediate root causes.

Goals: 1) reduce retry amplification during short upstream slowdowns, 2) provide an on-call-safe escape-hatch to steer specific customer traffic to a prioritized admission lane, 3) increase observability so SREs/SEs can make informed in-incident decisions without code changes.

Proposed approach: Implement a multi-part change: (A) Grace-window circuit-breaker semantics: instead of immediately increasing circuit score on the first N failures, apply a 10s sliding grace window that counts only sustained error rates above threshold before tripping. This permits transient spikes to recover without hard-routing changes. (B) Retry-suppression token: attach a short-lived header (X-RW-Retry-Suppress) for internal gateways to suppress client-side hedged retries when we detect amplification patterns. (C) Customer fast-path flagging: add an admission router flag that temporarily lowers queueing thresholds for flagged tenant IDs and routes them to a small warm pool reserved for escalations. (D) Observability/UI: Console endpoint with per-tenant 'escalation mode' marker and a dashboard panel showing grace-window triggers, suppressed retries, and fast-path occupancy.

Root cause hypothesis: client retry storms + synchronous admission policies amplified transient backend latency into service-wide 5xx waves. Existing mechanisms either over-react (trip too quickly) or under-protect high-priority customers.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Longer grace windows reduce false-positive trips but increase the time before we isolate a legitimately failing backend. We chose a conservative 10s default with per-route tunables. 2) Fast-path reduces latency for flagged customers but increases isolation risk; the pool size is intentionally small and subject to autoscaling guardrails. 3) Retry-suppression requires changes across edge and SDKs; we implement suppression opportunistically at our gateways first and later expose SDK guidance.

Progress updates:
- 2026-02-13: Spike implementation and prototype circuit-window logic completed (Arjun). Local integration tests show reduced trip rate on synthetic jittered error traces.
- 2026-02-15: Design review with SRE and Product (notes attached). Decided to use header-based suppression to avoid client SDK changes in the hot path (SRE signoff: Diego Rivera).
- 2026-02-17: PR #4982 opened for admission-router changes and new grace-window circuit state machine (PR link below).
- 2026-02-19: End-to-end staging run with 3 tenants simulating retry storms. Fast-path prevented two tenants from being impacted while non-flagged tenants experienced isolated degradation. Observability panels validated.
- 2026-02-22: Security review: no encryption or KMS changes needed. Security requested audit logs for any fast-path toggles (added).
- 2026-02-24: Canaries ready for controlled rollout to prod-1 region. Preparing runbook and customer communication templates.

Testing plan: unit tests for circuit logic, integration harness with synthetic client retry driver, staging soak with tenant-weighted load, and dark launch of X-RW-Retry-Suppress header on 1% of traffic. Acceptance criteria below.

Rollout plan: 1) Dark launch grace-window in runtime-1.24 canary with telemetry only. 2) Enable retry-suppression header handling in gateways and log toggles. 3) Enable per-tenant fast-path behind feature flag; reserve pool at 2% capacity initially. 4) Runbook: SREs may toggle fast-path for customer on-call; toggles recorded in audit logs. 5) If any regressions, roll back feature flag and revert admission-router configuration.

Customer comms: Draft saved for customer-bridge teams. Template includes symptom explanation, mitigation steps we performed, and a recommended client SDK update timeline for retry-suppression semantics.

Post-incident actions: update SDK docs with recommended retry jitter/backoff patterns, instrument more granular per-route latency percentiles, and create a retrospective for improving route-level defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Grace-window circuit prevents at least 70% of transient trips in staged test workload without increasing sustained error exposure
Retry-suppression header propagated and honored by gateway; suppression events appear in logs and dashboard
Console shows per-tenant escalation mode and fast-path pool occupancy; SREs can toggle per-tenant flag via UI
Feature flag rollout tested in prod-1 canary for 48 hours with no elevated 5xx rate attributable to the change
Audit log entries recorded for all fast-path toggles during rollout
decisions: Use 10s default grace-window with per-route override rather than global 30s window
Implement retry-suppression via internal header first to avoid SDK rollouts during initial mitigation
Reserve small (2-5%) warm pool capacity per-region for fast-path rather than unbounded routing priority
Require audit logging for fast-path toggles before rollout to all regions
notes: SRE recommended additional tracing tags for correlated retry chains (trace.parent_retry_id)
Product requested we expose a read-only escalation status API for customer success teams
Design and Console teams suggested a simple 'Escalation' badge on the tenant dashboard to avoid runbook navigation during incidents
postmortem_todo: Document SDK retry guidance; tune default grace-window per-workload; schedule retro with Sales/CS for customer communication improvements
customer_story: Customer ACME reported 20% failed requests during brief backend GC cycles. We enabled fast-path for their tenant for 45 minutes which restored stable traffic and allowed engineering to patch the upstream without requiring a forced customer-side retry change
